title: Incident becomes a rule: a catalog that learns from production
summary: After a UX incident in a shipped AI feature, an agent works out whether an existing rule was broken or a rule was missing. A broken rule becomes a bug with a named test. A missing rule becomes a proposed constraint with a level, a reason, and a test, ready for the catalog.

persona.role: Engineer writing the postmortem for an AI feature that misbehaved
persona.context: A user pressed stop and the agent carried on. The team adopted the interruption-cancel pattern, so either their code broke a rule or the rule did not exist.
persona.goal: A postmortem action that is a rule with a test, not a paragraph of lessons learned.

trigger: They paste an incident summary to the agent and ask: "Was this supposed to be impossible?"

advantage.claim: Every incident can end as a rule with a test, and every adopter hears about it through their pin.
advantage.why_it_holds: Constraints are atomic, versioned, and carry a rationale, so an incident maps onto one or onto none, and a new one is a small reviewable diff. Guidelines and pattern galleries are revised editorially; spec-driven workflows write their rules per project, so one team's incident teaches no one else.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A scratch project to hold the proposal.

steps.action: Incident A: "A user pressed Stop while the agent was sending follow-up emails. The button changed to Cancelling, then the progress indicator came back and two more emails went out." Find the pattern that governs this.

input.query: the user pressed stop but the agent kept going and sent two more emails

steps.expect: interruption-cancel ranked first, with its MUST statements.

steps.action: Decide whether an existing rule forbids what happened in incident A.
steps.expect: Yes: no-silent-continuation. The conclusion is an implementation bug, and the agent names the test that should have failed.

steps.action: Incident B: "On a phone, the task output pushed the stop control off screen. The user could not find it while the agent was running." Find the pattern that governs this.

input.query: the stop button scrolled off screen while the agent was running

steps.action: Read every constraint of the pattern, including SHOULD and MAY, which search does not return.
Decide whether an existing rule covers incident B. If none does, draft the missing rule.
steps.expect: The agent states which constraints it considered and why none requires the control to stay reachable while work runs, then drafts one constraint: id, level, category, statement, rationale, verification.

uses.change: The incident in two sentences, the drafted constraint as JSON, the version bump it requires and why, the test name that would prove it, and which adopters it affects.

steps.expect: A proposal the catalog owner can accept, change, or reject in one reading.

steps.action: Send the proposal to the catalog through a channel built for a missing or wrong rule.
steps.expect: An issue form that asks for the incident, the pattern, the proposed constraint, and the suggested level.

success.criterion: A covered incident is attributed to the rule that forbids it.
success.check: The s2 conclusion names no-silent-continuation and a test name starting with that id.

success.criterion: An uncovered incident yields a well-formed constraint.
success.check: The JSON in PROPOSAL.md has a kebab-case id not already in the contract, a level, a category, a statement containing the RFC 2119 keyword matching the level, a rationale, and a verification.

success.criterion: The version bump is classified correctly.
success.check: PROPOSAL.md says major if the drafted rule is MUST or MUST_NOT, and minor if it is SHOULD, SHOULD_NOT, or MAY.

success.criterion: The proposal legislates only through the contract.
success.check: The new requirement appears only as the drafted constraint. PROPOSAL.md's prose explains it and adds no further MUST or SHOULD.

gaps.summary: There is nowhere to send a proposed rule. The only issue link is a generic problem report.
gaps.evidence: The repository has no .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE directory. ISSUE_URL in site/lib/site.ts pre-fills where, what happened, and what you expected.
gaps.fix: Add an issue form for a missing or wrong rule: incident, pattern id, proposed constraint, suggested level.

gaps.summary: A changed hash says that a contract changed, not what changed or why.
gaps.evidence: Contracts carry a version and a hash and no change record. See the pin-and-drift-watch journey.
gaps.fix: Generate a change record per contract at build time and let an entry link to the issue that motivated it.

automation.schedule: On demand, per incident. As a regression check, run with the two fixture incidents after any change to interruption-cancel.
automation.notes: The runner never edits a contract. Accepting a proposal is the owner's decision and goes through /new-pattern or a contract revision with the bump the proposal names. Replace the two fixture incidents with a real one for real use.
